clue.text: Construction in Kensington reminiscent of one close to Victoria

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband, the person closest to her
reminiscent and memorial both describe what calls the past to mind

explanation.surface: A building in a smart London district recalls someone dear to the old Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The ALBERT MEMORIAL is the ornate Gothic monument to Prince Albert in Kensington Gardens, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The monument is a famous Victorian structure standing in Kensington Gardens, so it is a construction there.

clue.text: Bookmaker who makes a life for himself?

parts.note: auto- is the prefix meaning self, as in automatic
a biographer writes a life story

explanation.surface: A betting man somehow creates a living for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a betting shop, but it means a maker of books; 'for' lets the self prefix stand in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer produces books, so the one who writes their own life story is a maker of a book.

clue.text: Splinter in the saddle makes one lose control

parts.note: to splinter is to break into pieces
a rider in the saddle is said to be up, as a jockey is

explanation.surface: A sliver of wood under a rider's seat makes them lose their grip on the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: To break someone up is to make them collapse helplessly with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking someone up means reducing them to uncontrollable laughter or distress.

clue.text: Canon's cycle

definitions.meaning: a canon in music is a piece where voices enter one after another with the same tune, like 'Frere Jacques'
a cycle is a complete circuit or series that comes back to its start

explanation.surface: A churchman's bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical canon sung by staggered voices is the same form as a catch, and a cycle is a full circuit or turn.

clue.text: Indian radio operator held up desert army

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word for the radio operator is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator
to rat is to desert one's side
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An Indian wireless man was delayed by an army that went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahrattas were a warrior people of western India; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mahratta is a member of a people of western India, so the word names an Indian.

clue.text: Proposal to bring it up within a month

indicators.note: within says the turned word sits inside the word for a month

parts.note: a moon is a lunar month

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone suggests raising a matter during the next four weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the pronoun round in this down clue; a moon is a lunar month, and 'within' sets the turned letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is a formal proposal put to a meeting for debate and a vote.

clue.text: Recovery following run-out for a duck after a good shot

definitions.text: Recovery following run-out for a duck after a good shot

parts.words: Recovery following run-out for a duck after a good shot
parts.note: reads like a cricket batsman's comeback after being dismissed for no score, but describes a gundog fetching a duck the shooter has brought down

explanation.surface: A batsman bounces back after being run out without scoring, then hitting a fine stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought and a run-out a dismissal; here the duck is the bird, the shot from a gun, and the run-out a dog's dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching back a downed bird is what a gundog does, a recovery of game.

clue.text: How to get rid of lots of conflict about university

definitions.text: How to get rid of lots

indicators.note: about says the word for conflict goes round the abbreviation for university

parts.note: action is fighting, as in 'killed in action'

explanation.surface: A way of ending a lot of fighting around a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Lots are the numbered items in a sale room, so getting rid of lots is selling them off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale by bidding disposes of goods offered as numbered lots.

clue.text: Tatler writer in a frenzy about no, good print

parts.note: Richard Steele founded and wrote for The Tatler, the 18th-century periodical
N is an abbreviation for no, as in 'Y/N'
raving means wild with frenzy

explanation.surface: A society-magazine columnist rants about a worthless picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link meaning 'concerning'; the pieces run in order: STEELE, then N and G, then RAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: An image printed from an engraved metal plate is a kind of print.

clue.text: Old weapon the heartless butcher ordered

indicators.note: ordered means these letters are put into a new arrangement
heartless means the middle letter of the word the is taken out

explanation.surface: The cruel slaughterman ordered an ancient weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops H, the middle of THE, leaving TE; 'ordered' rearranges TE plus BUTCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet was a medieval siege engine that hurled stones, a weapon of old warfare.

clue.text: Ancient historian America ignored is silent

indicators.note: ignored means the abbreviation for America is left out of the historian's name

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian
US is America

explanation.surface: An old chronicler who overlooked the New World stays quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or understood without words, so it describes something left silent.

clue.text: A king sleeping gets very hot

annotationWithheld.why: A king sleeping gets very hot: B(A K)ED needs 'sleeping' to give BED and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: A king sleeping gets very hot

clue.text: One of the oldest diggers found spring in Lincoln

indicators.note: in places the word for spring inside the nickname of Lincoln

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
a spring is a source or origin

explanation.surface: A very old excavator turns up a source of water in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Diggers is slang for Australians, and the original inhabitants of Australia are the oldest of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal Australians are the continent's first people, and digger is slang for an Australian.

clue.text: The number of a colleague on the other side

definitions.meaning: a counterpart in another organisation is one's '... number'

explanation.surface: A coworker's phone number is across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart doing the same job elsewhere is called an opposite number; and facing across means placed on the far side.

clue.text: Parking inside this gate, abandoned busy junction

indicators.note: inside says the parking letter goes within the words this gate
abandoned means behaving wildly, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: With a car park inside it, this gate is deserted at a busy road crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a famously tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England; P goes into THISGATE and the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle of interweaving roads at a motorway interchange is called a spaghetti junction.

clue.text: Drive from a rendezvous

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: A road trip starts from a meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and avenue are both names for a road, often a tree-lined one.

clue.text: Scout, having embarked, at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boy scout who has boarded a ship is out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford University a scout is a college servant who makes the students' beds.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford college servant, called a scout, tidies rooms and makes beds.

clue.text: Try again to get nurse to swallow jelly, for example

indicators.note: to swallow means the word for nurse takes the explosive inside it

parts.note: to nurse a child is to rear it
jelly is slang for gelignite, an example of high explosive, HE

explanation.surface: Trying to make a nurse take a dessert again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly' looks like dessert; it is gelignite, a high explosive (HE).
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case is to try it again in court.

clue.text: This alien set about English

indicators.note: set about means the jumbled letters are placed around the abbreviation for English
alien means strange, so the letters of This are made strange

explanation.surface: A foreigner has attacked the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' scrambles This into HIST, which 'set about' wraps round. Hengist was a Germanic chieftain who led the invasion of Britain in the 5th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Hengist was a foreign invader who, by legend, attacked the native Britons and founded Kent.

clue.text: Grub enthusiast trapping unknown pest in hothouse

indicators.note: trapping means the unknown letter is caught between the two words

parts.note: grub is food, a meal
a bug is an enthusiast, as in 'the travel bug'
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A food fan catches an unidentified insect in the greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealybugs are sap-sucking insects that infest greenhouse plants.

clue.text: Asian mountain I drag my feet up

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words for I and drag my feet are read upwards

parts.note: to lag is to drag one's feet

explanation.surface: Slowly I climb an Asian peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads I and the foot-dragging word upwards, giving GALI; a ben is a Scottish mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, a region of South Asia.

clue.text: Natural medicine

definitions.meaning: natural here means unaffected, plain and artless
a herbal remedy made from one plant was called a ...

explanation.surface: Herbal remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and unaffected is a sense of natural; an old word for a herbal remedy from one plant is also this.

clue.text: A belief that's universally shared?

parts.note: not a belief everyone holds, but one holding that God is shared out through the whole universe

explanation.surface: A conviction held by everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine identifies God with the universe, so divinity is spread through all things.

clue.text: Native leader wearing old garment in Pacific kingdom

indicators.note: wearing means the leading letter has the old garment around it

parts.note: a toga was a garment of ancient Rome

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Native

explanation.surface: A local chief in a Roman robe in a South Seas monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Title role from libretto's Callas part

indicators.note: part means the answer is a portion of the letters of the words

explanation.surface: The lead in an opera, taken from the text, is Maria Callas's role.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas was famous as Tosca, the title role of Puccini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the heroine who gives Puccini's opera its name.

clue.text: Dispatch a letter, perhaps. I have sent back to court

indicators.note: sent back means the contraction for I have is turned round

parts.note: I have is contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Post a note? I've returned it to the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not mail but one who lets, here a lodger or tenant who is put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out a tenant or lodger is to evict them, a 'letter' read as one who lets a room.

clue.text: Painstaking crook up to no good is Asian

indicators.note: crook is Australian slang for bad or unwell, so the letters are put wrong

explanation.surface: A careful swindler is up to mischief, being from South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' scrambles the long word, and the abbreviation for no good is what is left over once the nationality is formed; 'up to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a person from Pakistan, a country of South Asia.

clue.text: Working in a black market?

parts.note: not illegal trading, but working while a strike has 'blacked' a workplace, which trade unionists regard as scabbing

explanation.surface: Doing business on the illegal market.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing picket lines to keep working during a dispute defeats the strike.
